evidence: Lower bound: Heise states, “While turnover in 1964 was 7,000 pounds, by 1970 it had risen to 50,000 pounds and by 1976 to 739,000 pounds.” https://www.heise.de/en/news/An-impossible-life-has-come-to-an-end-On-the-death-of-Dame-Stephanie-Shirley-10519340.html Using the Federal Reserve annual-average spot rate of 1.8048 USD/GBP for 1976, £739,000 = $1,333,747, below the 1976 nominal bar of $1,767,394. Upper bound: First Monday states, “FI grew and thrived, by 1979 revenue was £2.5 million, having doubled since 1977.” https://firstmonday.org/ojs/index.php/fm/article/download/13883/11743 Using the 1979 annual-average spot rate of 2.1224 USD/GBP, £2.5 million = $5,306,000, above the 1979 bar of $2,255,058. FX source (annual U.S. dollars per pound): https://fred.stlouisfed.org/data/AEXUSUK

Lower bound: Milwaukee Journal Sentinel states, “The company's growth, at least initially, wasn't explosive: By 1990, it had sales of $1.7 million and 29 employees.” $1.7 million is below the 1990 nominal bar of $4,059,725. Upper bound: the same source states, “Sales took off, reaching $18 million in 1995 - a tenfold increase in five years.” $18 million is above the 1995 nominal bar of $4,733,757. https://archive.jsonline.com/news/wisconsin/32597729.html

Lower bound: Encyclopedia.com states, “In 1972 she quit her job with GE and set up her new business in the spare bedroom of her apartment using her $300 advance from Halcyon and a $2,000 commission check from GE.” This sourced founding year is the permitted below-crossing lower bound. https://www.encyclopedia.com/education/economics-magazines/kurtzig-sandra-l Upper bound: Entrepreneur states, “The system was an instant hit, and ASK sales soared from $2.8 million in 1979 to $39 million in 1983, making it the 11th-fastest-growing company in the country between 1978 and 1982.” The 1979 revenue of $2.8 million is above the 1979 nominal bar of $2,255,058. https://www.entrepreneur.com/growing-a-business/sandra-kurtzig/197656

Lower bound: FundingUniverse's key dates state, “1986: Durachemie is sold to Cyanamid; Hexal Chemie GmbH & Co. KG is launched.” This sourced founding year is the permitted below-crossing lower bound. Upper bound: the same source states, “By 1988, the company's revenues had topped the equivalent of EUR 28 million.” https://www.fundinguniverse.com/company-histories/hexal-ag-history/ Because the source restates pre-euro revenue as a euro equivalent, I reconstructed the contemporaneous amount at the irrevocable rate €1 = DEM 1.95583 (https://www.ecb.europa.eu/press/pr/date/1998/html/pr981231_2.en.html): €28 million equivalent = DEM 54,763,240. At the 1988 annual-average spot rate of 1.756225 DEM/USD, that is $31,182,360, above the 1988 nominal bar of $3,674,564.
